appraisal_events.evidence: Après le passage de Mme de Villeparisis, « un salut sec abaissa son menton, elle ne me tendit même pas la main et ne m'a jamais reparlé depuis » ; le narrateur explique ensuite « de quels dépits amoureux, de quels échecs de snobisme étaient faits l'apparente hauteur, l'anti-snobisme universellement admis de la princesse Sherbatoff », et conclut que « les durs sont des faibles dont on n'a pas voulu ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator stages her cut of him only to unmask it: her celebrated hauteur and indifference to worldly vanity are declared to be the residue of social rebuffs, so the passage decisively lowers her even though the little clan closes ranks behind her reputation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « M. de Charlus ne se doutait pas… », les Verdurin tiennent loin de lui des propos tout autres que ceux qu'il imagine, ses audaces « faisai[en]t sourire en cachette », et « M. de Charlus vivait dupé comme le poisson qui croit que l'eau où il nage s'étend au delà du verre de son aquarium », guetté par « le pisciculteur, à Paris, [qui] sera Mme Verdurin ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator organizes the long central movement around Charlus's blindness: the flattering pavilion he imagines in the Verdurins' minds is doubled by a hostile invisible one, and he is framed as an unwitting creature already marked for expulsion.

status_effects.explanation: Her reputed strength and disdain for flattery are explicitly rewritten as failed snobbery and wounded vanity, a plain narratorial demolition.

He is silently and permanently dropped by the princess, and the Verdurins in chorus forbid him even to attempt a civility, so he is locally shut out of her regard; the parallel anecdote of the homme remarquable repeats the exclusion.
The narrator makes him ridiculous through unawareness: he takes the académicien's complaisance for natural kindness and believes his own performances go innocently received.

His standing in the little clan is shown to rest on nothing he controls: he is gossiped about behind his back and his position depends on a patronne who is prefigured as the fish-farmer who will one day pull him out.

ambiguities: The opening episode can be read either as a snub whose target is the narrator (cut by the princess, then warned off by the Verdurins) or as an exposure whose target is the princess; the evaluative weight of the passage falls on her unmasking, so the narrator's loss is recorded only as a secondary exclusion effect.

The Charlus movement carries real countervailing notes — the académicien's genuine amabilité, his effective advocacy for Morel, and the closing concession that « M. de Charlus était très intelligent » despite his « habitudes mondaines ridicules » — but these are subordinated to the sustained aquarium-and-pavilion frame of blindness, so the event is read as negative rather than mixed.
